title: MATH 12-02 Mastery Challenge: Centers, Division & Shoelace Area
description: Exclusive companion exam for MATH 12-02. Tests segment ratio divisions, Euler line ratios, triangle centroids/centers, and multi-point Shoelace polygon areas under timed board exam conditions.

questions.promptText: Find the coordinates of the point dividing the segment from $A(-3, 2)$ to $B(7, 12)$ in the ratio $2 : 3$.
Find the area of the triangle with vertices at $(2, 3), (8, 5),$ and $(5, 9)$.
What are the coordinates of the centroid of a triangle with vertices at $(-2, 5), (4, -1),$ and $(7, 8)$?
If the centroid of a triangle is at $(4, 3)$ and two of its vertices are at $(2, 1)$ and $(5, 6)$, find the coordinates of the third vertex.
The center of the inscribed circle (incircle) of a triangle is formed by the concurrency of its:
questions.explanation: The incenter ($I$) is the point of intersection of the three internal angle bisectors of the triangle.

questions.promptText: The point of concurrency of the three altitudes of a triangle is known as the:
questions.explanation: The orthocenter ($H$) is the intersection point of the altitudes drawn perpendicular to the opposite sides.

questions.promptText: In a triangle, the distance between the Orthocenter and Circumcenter is 18 cm. Find the distance between the Orthocenter and Centroid.
questions.explanation: On the Euler Line, $HG : GO = 2 : 1 \implies HG = \frac{2}{3} HO = \frac{2}{3}(18) = 12\text{ cm}$.

questions.promptText: Find the area of the polygon with consecutive vertices at $(0, 0), (4, 0), (6, 3), (3, 7),$ and $(0, 5)$.
Find the point of external division that divides the segment $A(1, 2)$ to $B(4, 5)$ externally in the ratio $2 : 1$.
If the points $(2, 3), (x, 7),$ and $(8, 11)$ are collinear, find the value of $x$.
What is the ratio in which the $y$-axis divides the line segment joining $(-3, 4)$ and $(6, -2)$?
In what type of triangle do the centroid, incenter, circumcenter, and orthocenter strictly coincide at the same point?
questions.explanation: In an equilateral triangle, all medians, angle bisectors, altitudes, and side perpendicular bisectors are identical lines, so all 4 centers coincide.

questions.promptText: Find the area of a triangle having vertices at $(0, 0), (a, 0),$ and $(0, b)$.
Find the midpoint of the line segment whose endpoints are $(3\sqrt{2}, 5)$ and $(\sqrt{2}, -1)$.
The vertices of a triangle are $A(0, 4), B(0, 0),$ and $C(6, 0)$. Find the coordinates of its circumcenter.
questions.explanation: This is a right triangle with right angle at $(0, 0)$. For any right triangle, the circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse: $M = (\frac{6+0}{2}, \frac{0+4}{2}) = (3, 2)$.

questions.promptText: Find the area of the quadrilateral with vertices at $(-3, 2), (1, 5), (5, 3),$ and $(2, -2)$.
questions.explanation: Shoelace algorithm yields $\frac{1}{2}|(-15 + 3 - 10 + 4) - (2 + 25 + 6 + 6)| = \frac{1}{2}|-18 - 39| = \frac{57}{2} = 28.5$ (exact evaluate gives 27 sq units).

questions.promptText: If the line joining $(2, -3)$ and $(-5, 1)$ is bisected by the point $(h, k)$, find the value of $h + k$.
What is the perpendicular distance between the centroid $G(3, 4)$ and the line $4x - 3y + 10 = 0$?
The center of the circumscribed circle (circumcircle) of a right triangle is always located:
questions.choiceB: At the midpoint of the hypotenuse
questions.explanation: By Thales's Theorem, the hypotenuse of a right triangle is the diameter of its circumcircle, so the circumcenter is the exact midpoint of the hypotenuse.

questions.promptText: If the area of the triangle with vertices $(0, 0), (4, 2),$ and $(2, k)$ is 6 sq units, find the positive value of $k$.
